---
title: "Charts"
description: >
  kit_plotly_style(): give plotly charts the KIT look so they match the app.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Pass a plotly chart drawn by kits (for example `plot(item, type = "category")`) to `kit_plotly_style()` as the last step:
font, axis lines, grid lines, background, title, legend, color bar, hover labels, and toolbar all take the KIT look.
**It changes only the look, not the data**: points, lines, axis ranges, ticks, and hover text stay as they are.

## Before and after

Left: the original chart. Right: after `kit_plotly_style()`.

**Category probability curves** (small multiples: the black frame around each panel becomes a light line, and there are no frames inside frames)

**Response design chart** (heat map: switched to the KIT color scale)

<img class="kit-shot" src="figures/chart-design.jpg" alt="Response design chart: the original color scale on the left, KIT's light lime to KIT green on the right" width="1400">

**Wright map**

<img class="kit-shot" src="figures/chart-wright.jpg" alt="Wright map: the original look on the left, after styling on the right" width="1400">

The lowest value in a heat map is not white, so 0% cells and cells that were not administered (blank) are easy to tell apart.

<img class="kit-shot" src="figures/chart-heat-zero.jpg" alt="Heat map: 0% is a very light lime, cells with no data are white" width="1000">

## How to use it

```{r}
library(kitDesign)

p <- plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~wave, y = ~score, split = ~cohort,
                     type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers")
p <- plotly::layout(p, title = "各世代的分數中位數")  # "Median score by cohort"
kit_plotly_style(p)
```

## With kits and kitsUI: the order

1. Draw the chart with kits' `plot()`.
2. Recolor with kitsUI: `kit_chart_categorical()`, `kit_chart_role()`.
3. Switch to Chinese labels with kitsUI: `kit_chart_zh()`. **This must come before `kit_plotly_style()`**:
   `kit_plotly_style()` makes titles bold (`<b>`), and after that the original English titles can no longer be recognized.
4. `kit_plotly_style()` last.

```{r}
p <- plot(item, type = "category")              # 1. kits
p <- kit_chart_zh(kit_chart_categorical(p))     # 2–3. kitsUI: recolor, Chinese labels
kit_plotly_style(p)                             # 4. last
```

Styling the same chart twice gives the same result as styling it once. Colors set by kits or kitsUI are kept; only
plotly's own default colors are replaced with Okabe–Ito (colorblind-friendly).

## Common options

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `legend = "auto"` | Moves the legend to the bottom when it has more than 4 entries or is too long, or when the chart is narrower than 600px (phones); also `"bottom"`, `"right"`, `"keep"` |
| `colorscale = FALSE` | Keeps the heat map's original color scale |
| `filename = "kit-chart"` | File name for the toolbar's "Download as PNG" |
| `font_size = 15` | Body text size (px); other sizes are derived from it |
| `brand = ` | Heat map color scale follows the brand (see [Using another brand](brand.html)) |

Colors: categorical colors `kit_chart_colors()`, reference lines `kit_chart_neutral()`, continuous values `kit_chart_sequential()`.
